title: A/P Unpaid Invoices: a vendor credit belongs to its return or vendor
custom_preconds:
Setup file (for Claude sessions; a tester does not need it)

Preconditions

  • You are signed in as a user with the "Admin" role, with {Location-A} as your current location.
    For example: {Location-A} is Staging Heavy Duty - 9919.
  • The organization has open documents in these reports at two locations, {Location-A} and {Location-B}, and you are enrolled at both; {Location-A}'s name comes first in A to Z order.
    For example: {Location-A} is Staging Heavy Duty - 9919 and {Location-B} is Staging Lethbridge - 4310.
  • Vendor {Vendor-A}, whose own location is {Location-A}, has two unused vendor credits: {Vendor-credit-A} from a vendor return made at {Location-B}, and {Vendor-credit-B} not from a vendor return.
    For example: {Vendor-A} is ZZAUTOTEST S5-17 Credit Home.
  • Starting screen: Reports > Finance > A/P Unpaid Invoices is open in a desktop browser window 1440 px wide, as opened from the Reports menu, with the Vendor filter showing {Vendor-A} ticked and its group expanded.
  • If any record above is missing, mark this test Blocked: "setup not done".
custom_steps:
1. Read the Location of {Vendor-credit-A} and {Vendor-credit-B}.
  2. In the Location menu, untick {Location-A}.
  3. Expand {Vendor-A}'s group.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Step 1: {Vendor-credit-A} shows {Location-B} (the return's location); {Vendor-credit-B} shows {Location-A} (the vendor's location, as today).
  • Step 2: the report narrows to {Location-B}.
  • Step 3: only {Vendor-credit-A} is listed.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "A/R and A/P Report Sorting, Export and Location Filter", Confluence 947650561, version 5 (21 Oct 2026, Chris Ward), read 22 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-11315, story SV-11535 (Story 5, Filters: customer or vendor, past due and location)

  • S5-R7: “which location an A/P row belongs to, stated per document (bill: its delivery; vendor credit from a return: the return; other vendor credits: the vendor).”
